system_description.narrative_title: A Fractured, Interconnected Global Order Under Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, tightly coupled process where great-power competition, regional wars, and market stresses interact and amplify one another. Diplomatic spectacle and limited cooperation (notably US–China talks) coexist with kinetic conflicts (Ukraine, the Middle East), energy shocks, and a re-pricing of risk across bond and credit markets—feeding domestic political fragmentation and economic pain. These feedbacks make shocks in one domain (oil, missiles, market sentiment) propagate rapidly across the whole system, producing cascading instability and episodic management rather than durable resolution.
system_description.scope: State and non-state military conflicts and deterrence dynamics; great-power diplomacy and rivalry (US, China, Russia, Iran); global energy and commodity flows; financial markets (sovereign bonds, private equity/credit); domestic politics and elections that interact with international policy; technology and supply-chain vulnerabilities.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-technical system (globalized economy, climate and energy systems, and transnational information/technology networks).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and capital flows
Energy and commodity supply chains (oil, diesel, LNG, electricity/AI power demand)

variables.name: U.S.–Iran military and diplomatic standoff
variables.description: An escalating military and diplomatic confrontation between the United States, Iran and regional actors is producing strikes, mediation shuttles, rejected ceasefire offers and sustained disruptions to Gulf energy flows and shipping.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain engaged in a high-intensity conventional and hybrid war marked by long-range strikes, drone campaigns and attacks on infrastructure that keep Europe’s security posture and allied support commitments in flux.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic competition
variables.description: The United States and China are locked in an expanding rivalry across trade, advanced technology (including AI), high-level diplomacy and regional security issues—illustrated by tariff negotiations, limited summit breakthroughs and persistent Taiwan-related tensions.

variables.name: Global bond and credit market stress
variables.description: A broad sell-off in government bonds, sharply higher yields and strains in private credit and private equity are tightening global financing conditions, disrupting markets and forcing policy recalibrations among central banks and investors.

variables.name: Alliance realignments and hybrid-security threats
variables.description: NATO members, regional partners and other states are recalibrating defence relationships, collective responses and base-security practices in the face of hybrid attacks, suspected foreign-linked incidents and new military partnerships across Europe and Asia.
